41	
42	    if ! command -v pueue &>/dev/null; then
43	        printf '%s%s%s\n' "$c_err" "pqsum: pueue not found in PATH" "$c_reset" >&2
44	        return 127
45	    fi
46	
47	    if ! command -v jq &>/dev/null; then
48	        printf '%s%s%s\n' "$c_err" "pqsum: jq not found in PATH" "$c_reset" >&2
49	        return 127
50	    fi
51	
52	    local requested_group="" idx arg
53	    for ((idx = 1; idx <= $#; idx++)); do
54	        arg="${@[$idx]}"
55	        case "$arg" in
56	            -g|--group)
57	                if (( idx < $# )); then
58	                    requested_group="${@[$((idx + 1))]}"
59	                fi
60	                ;;
61	            --group=*)
62	                requested_group="${arg#--group=}"
63	                ;;
64	        esac

67	    local pueue_json rc
68	    pueue_json="$(pueue status --json "$@")"

72	        return "$rc"

75	    local stats_json
76	    stats_json="$(jq -c --arg requested_group "$requested_group" '

78	          .status | keys[0];
79	
80	        def normalize_ts:
81	          sub("\\.[0-9]+"; "") as $ts
82	          | if ($ts | test("Z$")) then
83	              ($ts | sub("Z$"; "+0000"))
84	            elif ($ts | test("[+-][0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}$")) then
85	              ($ts | capture("(?<prefix>.*)(?<h>[+-][0-9]{2}):(?<m>[0-9]{2})$") | "\(.prefix)\(.h)\(.m)")
86	            else
87	              $ts
88	            end;
89	
90	        def to_epoch:
91	          normalize_ts
92	          | strptime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z")
93	          | mktime;
94	
95	        def done_seconds:
96	          if (.status | has("Done")) and (.status.Done.start != null) and (.status.Done.end != null) then
97	            ((.status.Done.end | to_epoch) - (.status.Done.start | to_epoch))
98	          else
99	            null
100	          end;
101	
102	        def pct($part; $total):

104	
105	        def fmt_pct($num):

107	
108	        def fmt_duration:

110	            "-"
111	          else

113	            | if $s < 60 then
114	                "\($s)s"
115	              elif $s < 3600 then
116	                "\(($s / 60 | floor))m \(($s % 60) | floor)s"
117	              else
118	                "\(($s / 3600 | floor))h \(((($s % 3600) / 60) | floor))m \(($s % 60) | floor)s"
119	              end
120	          end;
121	
122	        def status_map_to_string:
123	          if (length == 0) then
124	            "-"
125	          else
126	            (to_entries | sort_by(.key) | map("\(.key)=\(.value)") | join(", "))
127	          end;
128	
129	        (.tasks // {} | with_entries(.value |= del(.envs))) as $tasks
130	        | (.groups // {}) as $groups
131	        | ($tasks | to_entries | map(.value)) as $task_list
132	        | ($task_list | length) as $total
133	        | ($task_list | map(select(task_status == "Done")) | length) as $done
134	        | ($task_list | map(done_seconds) | map(select(. != null))) as $done_durations
135	        | ($done_durations | if length > 0 then (add / length) else null end) as $avg_done_sec
136	        | (pct($done; $total)) as $overall_pct
137	        | (
138	            if $requested_group != "" then
139	              if ($groups | has($requested_group)) or ($task_list | any((.group // "default") == $requested_group)) then
140	                [$requested_group]

142	                []
143	              end
144	            else
145	              ((($groups | keys_unsorted) + ($task_list | map(.group // "default"))) | unique | sort)
146	            end
147	          ) as $group_names
148	        | ($task_list | sort_by(task_status) | group_by(task_status)
149	            | map({
150	                status: (.[0] | task_status),
151	                count: length,
152	                pct_num: pct(length; $total),
153	                pct: fmt_pct(pct(length; $total))
154	              })
155	          ) as $status_rows
156	        | ($group_names | map(
157	            . as $group_name
158	            | ($task_list | map(select((.group // "default") == $group_name))) as $group_tasks
159	            | ($group_tasks | length) as $group_total
160	            | ($group_tasks | map(select(task_status == "Done")) | length) as $group_done
161	            | ($group_total - $group_done) as $group_remaining
162	            | ($group_tasks | map(done_seconds) | map(select(. != null))) as $group_durations
163	            | (
164	                $group_tasks
165	                | map(
166	                    [
167	                      .created_at,
168	                      (.status[]?.enqueued_at?),
169	                      (.status[]?.start?),
170	                      (.status[]?.end?)
171	                    ]
172	                    | map(select(. != null))
173	                    | map(to_epoch)
174	                  )
175	                | if length > 0 then add else [] end
176	              ) as $group_timestamps
177	            | ($group_timestamps | if length > 0 then min else null end) as $group_first_ts
178	            | ($group_timestamps | if length > 0 then max else null end) as $group_last_ts
179	            | (
180	                if $group_first_ts != null and $group_last_ts != null then
181	                  ($group_last_ts - $group_first_ts)
182	                else
183	                  null
184	                end
185	              ) as $group_spent_sec
186	            | ($group_durations | if length > 0 then (add / length) else null end) as $group_avg_sec
187	            | ($groups[$group_name].parallel_tasks // 1) as $group_parallel_raw
188	            | (
189	                if ($group_parallel_raw | type) == "number" and $group_parallel_raw > 0 then

191	                else
192	                  1
193	                end
194	              ) as $group_parallel_for_eta
195	            | ($group_tasks | sort_by(task_status) | group_by(task_status) | map({key: (.[0] | task_status), value: length}) | from_entries) as $group_status_map
196	            | (pct($group_done; $group_total)) as $group_pct
197	            | (

199	                  (if $group_total > 0 then 0 else null end)
200	                elif $group_avg_sec == null then
201	                  null
202	                else
203	                  (($group_remaining * $group_avg_sec) / $group_parallel_for_eta)
204	                end
205	              ) as $group_eta_sec
206	            | {
207	                group: $group_name,
208	                daemon: ($groups[$group_name].status // "N/A"),
209	                parallel: ($groups[$group_name].parallel_tasks // "-"),
210	                total: $group_total,
211	                done: $group_done,
212	                pct_num: $group_pct,
213	                pct_int: ($group_pct | round),
214	                pct: fmt_pct($group_pct),
215	                total_spent: ($group_spent_sec | fmt_duration),

217	                eta_sec: $group_eta_sec,
218	                eta: ($group_eta_sec | fmt_duration),
219	                statuses: ($group_status_map | status_map_to_string)

223	        | (if ($overall_eta_candidates | length) > 0 then ($overall_eta_candidates | max) else null end) as $overall_eta_sec

225	            overall: {
226	              total: $total,
227	              done: $done,
228	              progress_pct_num: $overall_pct,
229	              progress_pct_int: ($overall_pct | round),
230	              progress_pct: fmt_pct($overall_pct),
231	              avg_done: ($avg_done_sec | fmt_duration),
232	              eta_sec: $overall_eta_sec,
233	              eta: ($overall_eta_sec | fmt_duration)
234	            },
235	            status_rows: $status_rows,
236	            group_rows: $group_rows
237	          }
238	    ' <<< "$pueue_json")"
239	    rc=$?
240	    if (( rc != 0 )); then
241	        printf '%s%s%s\n' "$c_err" "pqsum: failed to summarize status JSON" "$c_reset" >&2
242	        return "$rc"
243	    fi

247	    fi

# CLI Tools Reference

All tools installed by this dotfiles project. The **Invocation** column is what gets pasted to the shell buffer by the `tools-picker` (Alt+T) and TV channel (`tv tools`). Tools with a trailing space need an argument before running.

> **Source of truth for the interactive pickers**: both `tv tools` and the fzf ZLE widget (Alt+T) parse this file at runtime.

---

## File & Search

| Command | Invocation | Description | Notes |
|---------|------------|-------------|-------|
| `rg` | `rg ` | Fast regex search (ripgrep) | `-l` files only, `-i` case-insensitive, `-t` by filetype |
| `fd` | `fd ` | Fast file finder | `-t f` files, `-t d` dirs, `-e ext` by extension |
| `bat` | `bat ` | cat with syntax highlighting | `--plain`, `--paging=never`, `-l` language |
| `eza` | `eza ` | Modern ls with git status | aliases: `ls`, `la`, `ll`, `lt`, `llt` |
| `fzf` | `fzf` | Interactive fuzzy finder | `Ctrl+T` files, `Ctrl+R` history, `Alt+C` cd |
| `yazi` | `yazi` | TUI file manager (cd on exit) | alias `y` for cd-on-exit wrapper |
| `glow` | `glow ` | Render Markdown in terminal | `glow -p` paged |
| `duckdb` | `duckdb ` | In-process SQL analytics | `.open file.db` to open, `.tables` to list |
| `rclone` | `rclone ` | Sync files to/from cloud storage | `rclone sync src dst` |

---

## Git & Diff

| Command | Invocation | Description | Notes |
|---------|------------|-------------|-------|
| `lazygit` | `lazygit` | Git TUI | alias `lg` |
| `gh` | `gh ` | GitHub CLI | `gh pr`, `gh issue`, `gh repo clone`, `gh run` |
| `delta` | `delta ` | Diff pager with syntax highlight | configured as default git pager |
| `diffnav` | `diffnav` | TUI diff navigator | `diffnav <file>` or pipe from `git diff` |
| `git-graph` | `git-graph` | Visual branch graph | `git-graph --all` |
| `gitleaks` | `gitleaks ` | Secret scanner | `gitleaks detect`, `gitleaks protect` |
| `pre-commit` | `pre-commit ` | Git hook manager | `pre-commit run --all-files`, `pre-commit install` |

---

## Sessions & Multiplexing

| Command | Invocation | Description | Notes |

```toml
# Custom tools cable channel for television (tv)
# Parses ~/.config/docs/tools/cli-tools.md at runtime — single source of truth.
#
# Usage:
#   tv tools                               (from shell)
#   prefix + U in tmux                     (popup)
#   Alt+T in zsh                           (opens fzf ZLE variant instead)
#
# Keybindings:
#   Enter      Execute selected tool immediately
#   Ctrl+/     Toggle preview panel
#
# Preview shows tldr page or --help output.

[metadata]
name = "tools"
description = "CLI tools quick-launch: select a tool to execute it"
requirements = ["awk"]

[source]
command = """
awk -F'|' '/^[[:space:]]*\\|[[:space:]]*`/ {
  inv=$3; sub(/^[[:space:]]*`/,"",inv); sub(/`[[:space:]]*$/,"",inv)
  desc=$4; sub(/^[[:space:]]*/,"",desc); sub(/[[:space:]]*/,"",desc)
  printf "%-22s  %s\\n", inv, desc
}' ~/.config/docs/tools/cli-tools.md
"""

[preview]
command = """
tool=$(printf '%s' '{split: :0}' | sed 's/ *$//')
if command -v tldr >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  tldr "$tool" 2>/dev/null || "$tool" --help 2>&1 | head -50
else
  "$tool" --help 2>&1 | head -50
fi
"""

[keybindings]
enter = "actions:exec"

[actions.exec]
description = "Execute selected tool"
command = "{split: :0}"
mode = "execute"

```

```zsh
# 11_tools_picker.zsh - Interactive CLI tools picker (fzf ZLE widget)
# Reads ~/.config/docs/tools/cli-tools.md for the tool list (deployed by chezmoi).
#
# Alt+T  →  open picker
#   Enter      paste invocation to shell buffer (you still press Enter to run)
#   Ctrl+E     execute the tool directly (good for TUI apps: btop, lazygit, etc.)
#   Ctrl+/     toggle preview panel (shows tldr or --help)
#
# The invocation for tools that need arguments has a trailing space,
# so pressing Enter pastes e.g. "rg " — cursor lands after the space,
# ready for you to type your arguments.

_TOOLS_DOC="${HOME}/.config/docs/tools/cli-tools.md"

# Bail silently if the data file hasn't been deployed yet or fzf is missing
[[ -f "$_TOOLS_DOC" ]] || return 0
command -v fzf &>/dev/null || return 0

# Parse the markdown tables into "INVOCATION<TAB>DESCRIPTION" lines.
# Tab separator preserves the trailing space in invocations like "rg ".
_tools_list() {
    awk -F'|' '/^[[:space:]]*\|[[:space:]]*`/ {
      inv=$3; sub(/^[[:space:]]*`/,"",inv); sub(/`[[:space:]]*$/,"",inv)
      desc=$4; sub(/^[[:space:]]*/,"",desc); sub(/[[:space:]]*/,"",desc)
      printf "%s\t%s\n", inv, desc
    }' "$_TOOLS_DOC"
}

# ZLE widget: opens fzf picker, pastes selected invocation to the shell command line.
tools-picker() {
    {
        exec </dev/tty
        exec <&1

        local selected
        selected=$(
            _tools_list | fzf \
                --ansi \
                --border \
                --prompt ' tools  ' \
                --header 'Enter: paste  Ctrl+E: execute  Ctrl+/: preview' \
                --delimiter=$'\t' \
                --with-nth=1,2 \
                --preview 'tool=$(printf "%s" {1} | awk "{print \$1}" | sed "s/ *$//"); (command -v tldr >/dev/null 2>&1 && tldr "$tool" 2>/dev/null) || "$tool" --help 2>&1 | head -50' \
                --preview-window='right:55%:wrap:hidden' \
                --bind='ctrl-/:toggle-preview' \
                --bind='ctrl-e:execute(eval $(printf "%s" {1} | awk "{print \$1}"))+abort'
        )

        zle reset-prompt >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
        [[ -z "$selected" ]] && return

        # Extract the invocation (field 1 before the tab), preserving trailing space
        local invocation
        invocation=$(printf '%s' "$selected" | cut -f1)

        # Paste to shell command line buffer without executing
        LBUFFER="${LBUFFER}${invocation}"
        zle redisplay
    }
}

zle -N tools-picker

# Alt+T (mnemonic: Tools)
# Alt+S = sesh-sessions, Alt+C = fzf cd — Alt+T is free
bindkey -M emacs '\et' tools-picker
bindkey -M viins '\et' tools-picker
bindkey -M vicmd '\et' tools-picker

```

=== TV cable channel ===
# Custom tools cable channel for television (tv)
# Parses ~/.config/docs/tools/cli-tools.md at runtime — single source of truth.
#
# Usage:
#   tv tools                               (from shell)
#   prefix + U in tmux                     (popup)
#   Alt+T in zsh                           (opens fzf ZLE variant instead)
#
# Keybindings:
#   Enter      Execute selected tool immediately
#   Ctrl+/     Toggle preview panel
#
# Preview shows tldr page or --help output.

[metadata]
name = "tools"
description = "CLI tools quick-launch: select a tool to execute it"
requirements = ["awk"]

[source]
command = """
awk -F'|' '/^[[:space:]]*\\|[[:space:]]*`/ {
  inv=$3; sub(/^[[:space:]]*`/,"",inv); sub(/`[[:space:]]*$/,"",inv)
  desc=$4; sub(/^[[:space:]]*/,"",desc); sub(/[[:space:]]*/,"",desc)
  printf "%-22s  %s\\n", inv, desc
}' ~/.config/docs/tools/cli-tools.md
"""

[preview]
command = """
tool=$(printf '%s' '{split: :0}' | sed 's/ *$//')
if command -v tldr >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  tldr "$tool" 2>/dev/null || "$tool" --help 2>&1 | head -50
else
  "$tool" --help 2>&1 | head -50
fi
"""

[keybindings]
enter = "actions:exec"

[actions.exec]
description = "Execute selected tool"
command = "{split: :0}"
mode = "execute"

# 11_tools_picker.zsh - Interactive CLI tools picker (fzf ZLE widget)
# Reads ~/.config/docs/tools/cli-tools.md for the tool list (deployed by chezmoi).
#
# Alt+T  →  open picker
#   Enter      paste invocation to shell buffer (you still press Enter to run)
#   Ctrl+E     execute the tool directly (good for TUI apps: btop, lazygit, etc.)
#   Ctrl+/     toggle preview panel (shows tldr or --help)
#
# The invocation for tools that need arguments has a trailing space,
# so pressing Enter pastes e.g. "rg " — cursor lands after the space,
# ready for you to type your arguments.

_TOOLS_DOC="${HOME}/.config/docs/tools/cli-tools.md"

# Bail silently if the data file hasn't been deployed yet or fzf is missing
[[ -f "$_TOOLS_DOC" ]] || return 0
command -v fzf &>/dev/null || return 0

# Parse the markdown tables into "INVOCATION<TAB>DESCRIPTION" lines.
# Tab separator preserves the trailing space in invocations like "rg ".
_tools_list() {
    awk -F'|' '/^[[:space:]]*\|[[:space:]]*`/ {
      inv=$3; sub(/^[[:space:]]*`/,"",inv); sub(/`[[:space:]]*$/,"",inv)
      desc=$4; sub(/^[[:space:]]*/,"",desc); sub(/[[:space:]]*/,"",desc)
      printf "%s\t%s\n", inv, desc
    }' "$_TOOLS_DOC"
}

# ZLE widget: opens fzf picker, pastes selected invocation to the shell command line.
tools-picker() {
    {
        exec </dev/tty
        exec <&1

        local selected
        selected=$(
            _tools_list | fzf \
                --ansi \
                --border \
                --prompt ' tools  ' \

### TMUX (Ctrl+B Prefix)

#### Prefix Bindings - Daily Workflow
| Binding | Action |

### Zellij Configuration

**Zellij starts in locked mode** — all keys pass through to inner applications by default.

| Key | Action |
|-----|--------|
| `Ctrl+G` | Unlock Zellij commands (default "Unlock-First" preset) |

**Note:** On first Zellij launch (without existing config), the setup wizard offers keybinding presets. Select "Unlock-First (non-colliding)" to avoid key conflicts with coding agents and vim-style applications. The config file is minimal and intentionally avoids defining custom keybindings beyond the unlock key.

To switch presets later:
- Default preset: `Ctrl+O` → `c`
- Unlock-First preset: `Ctrl+G` → `o` → `c`

**Settings:**
- `default_mode "locked"` — keys pass through by default
- `support_kitty_keyboard_protocol true` — proper Shift+Enter, Ctrl+Enter, etc.
- `session_serialization true` — session persistence like tmux-resurrect
- `mouse_mode true` — mouse support enabled

```text
1	# Dotfiles Repository
2	
3	Cross-platform dotfiles management using **chezmoi** for configuration files and **ansible** for system dependencies.
4	
5	## Maintaining README.md
6	
7	**IMPORTANT**: When adding or modifying configurations, update `README.md` to reflect changes:
8	
9	- **New config files**: Add to "What You Get > Config Files" section
10	- **New ansible roles/tools**: Add to "What You Get > Tools" section
11	- **New platforms**: Add to "Supported Platforms" table
12	- **Changed setup steps**: Update "Quick Setup" section
13	
14	Keep README.md concise and user-focused. Technical details belong in CLAUDE.md or docs/.
15	
16	## Maintaining Custom Aliases & Shell Functions
17	
18	**IMPORTANT**: When adding or modifying a custom alias or shell function in any `dot_config/zsh/` file, update `docs/zsh/aliases.md`:
19	
20	- **New entry**: add a row with the command name, type (`alias` or `function`), source file (relative to repo root), and a one-line description
21	- **Modified entry**: update the existing row to reflect changes
22	- **Removed entry**: delete the row
23	
24	This keeps `docs/zsh/aliases.md` as the single quick-reference for all custom shell shortcuts.
25	
26	## Maintaining Dockerfile
27	
28	**IMPORTANT**: When adding new chezmoi prompts in `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl`, also update `Dockerfile`:
29	
30	1. Add corresponding `ARG CHEZMOI_*` build argument
31	2. Add `--promptBool` or `--promptString` flag to the `chezmoi init` command
32	
33	This ensures Docker testing works with all configuration options.
34	
35	## Quick Start
36	
37	```bash
38	# Install ansible (if not already installed)
39	uv tool install ansible-core
40	ansible-galaxy collection install community.general
41	
42	# Apply dotfiles
43	chezmoi apply
44	
45	# Run ansible manually (from ~/.ansible directory)
46	cd ~/.ansible && ansible-playbook playbooks/macos.yml
47	```
48	
49	## Architecture
50	
51	```
52	chezmoi repo/
53	├── dot_* files               → ~/.* (config files)
54	├── dot_ansible/              → ~/.ansible/ (ansible playbooks)
55	├── run_once_before_*.tmpl    → bootstrap (runs once)
56	└── run_onchange_after_*.tmpl → ansible (runs on changes)
57	```
58	
59	Installation Order:
60	
61	```
62	1. Bootstrap (run_once_before) - installs Homebrew (macOS/Linux), uv, ansible, mise
63	2. chezmoi apply - deploys config files + ansible playbooks
64	3. Ansible (run_onchange_after) - runs on fresh install + when roles change
65	4. Brew bundle (run_onchange_after) - installs GUI apps if enabled
66	```
67	
68	### Auto-run Scripts
69	
70	| Script | Behavior |
71	|--------|----------|
72	| `run_once_before_00_bootstrap.sh.tmpl` | Installs Homebrew (macOS and Linux), uv, mise, ansible |
73	| `run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl` | Runs ansible with all tags |
74	| `run_onchange_after_30_brew_bundle.sh.tmpl` | Runs brew bundle (if `installBrewApps` is enabled, or on macOS if `installAiDesktopApps` is enabled) |
75	
76	The onchange script includes SHA256 hashes of all role files. It runs:
77	
78	- **Fresh install**: no previous hash state → triggers run
79	- **Updates**: any role's `tasks/main.yml` or `defaults/main.yml` changes → triggers run
80	
81	To force re-run all scripts:
82	
83	```bash
84	chezmoi state delete-bucket --bucket=scriptState
85	chezmoi apply
86	```
87	
88	## Chezmoi Commands
89	
90	```bash
91	chezmoi diff              # Preview changes
92	chezmoi apply             # Apply changes
93	chezmoi apply --dry-run   # Test without applying
94	chezmoi edit <file>       # Edit source file
95	chezmoi cd                # Go to source directory
96	```
97	
98	## Ansible Usage
99	
100	Ansible playbooks run automatically via `chezmoi apply` when playbook files change. For manual runs, use `~/.ansible/` directory:
101	
102	```bash
103	cd ~/.ansible
104	
105	# Full setup (macOS)
106	ansible-playbook playbooks/macos.yml
107	
108	# Full setup (Linux)
109	ansible-playbook playbooks/linux.yml
110	
111	# Specific tags only
112	ansible-playbook playbooks/macos.yml --tags "neovim,lazyvim_deps"
113	
114	# Skip tags requiring sudo
115	ansible-playbook playbooks/linux.yml --skip-tags "sudo"
116	
117	# Dry run
118	ansible-playbook playbooks/macos.yml --check
119	```

161	## No Root Mode (Linux)
162	
163	For Linux servers where you don't have sudo/root access, enable `noRoot = true` during `chezmoi init`:
164	
165	```bash
166	chezmoi init --force  # Answer "y" to "No sudo/root access" prompt
167	```
168	
169	This skips all tasks tagged with `[sudo]` (apt packages, system-level installations). Tools with user-level fallbacks are automatically installed to `~/.local/bin` instead.
170	
171	**User-level tools** (installed automatically without sudo):
172	
173	- **GitHub binaries**: neovim, ripgrep, fd, jq, just, bat, eza, delta, yazi, zellij, btop, gitleaks, lazygit, fzf, sesh, taplo, television
174	- **mise**: Node.js, Rust runtime management
175	- **Installers**: zoxide, starship, pre-commit, thefuck, tldr
176	- **cargo tools**: pueue
177	- **uv tools**: mlflow, sqlit-tui, tmuxp, etc.
178	- **llm tools**: ollama, litellm, llmfit, models
179	- **npm tools**: Claude Code, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Bitwarden CLI, etc.
180	
181	What you **won't get** without root:
182	
183	- zsh (needs `/etc/shells` for login shell)
184	- tmux, htop (require system libraries)
185	- direnv (apt only)
186	- Docker (kernel features, daemon)
187	- Ollama (system service install)
188	- System fonts (nerdfonts)
189	- Ruby and gem tools (ruby-build requires `libffi-dev` which needs sudo)
190	- build-essential, git, curl, wget, tree (assumed pre-installed)
191	
192	**Tip**: Ask your sysadmin to run: `sudo apt install git curl wget zsh tmux htop direnv build-essential tree`
193	
194	## Tmux Configuration
195	
196	The tmux config is modular under `dot_config/tmux/` (deployed to `~/.config/tmux/`), with `dot_tmux.conf` acting as a one-line shim at `~/.tmux.conf`. Structure: `tmux.conf` (entry point + theme selector), `common.conf` (plugins, general options, terminal compat), `keybindings.conf` (all binds + popup menu), `theme.catppuccin.conf` (default, top status bar), `theme.tmux2k.conf` (alternative, bottom bar).
197	
198	Theme selection priority: `$TMUX_THEME` env var → `@theme_variant` tmux option → default `catppuccin`. Switch at runtime with `prefix + M-c` (Catppuccin) or `prefix + M-t` (tmux2k). See `docs/tools/tmux/` (README, keybindings, themes, vim) for full details, including a troubleshooting note on the tmux2k bandwidth segment (`18446744073709551615K` = uint64 underflow).
199	
200	The Catppuccin status bar is **responsive**: `responsive.sh` + a `client-resized` hook dynamically adjust which modules are shown based on terminal width (>= 120 full, 80-119 medium, < 80 minimal). This makes the status bar usable on mobile terminals. See `docs/tools/tmux/themes.md` for details.
201	
202	### Key Settings for Coding Agents
203	
204	- `extended-keys always` + `terminal-features 'xterm*:extkeys'` -- forwards Shift+Enter, Ctrl+Enter, etc. through tmux to inner applications (Claude Code, Neovim, etc.)
205	- `escape-time 0` -- eliminates ESC delay for Neovim
206	- `set-clipboard on` -- OSC 52 clipboard (works over SSH)
207	- `allow-passthrough on` -- OSC passthrough for terminal images
208	- macOS terminals must send Option as Meta/Esc+ for `M-` keybindings (theme switching, layouts, fine resize). Ghostty/cmux: `macos-option-as-alt = left` (managed in `dot_config/ghostty/config`). See `docs/tools/ghostty.md`.
209	
210	### Tmux Keybindings
211	
212	| Binding | Action |
213	|---------|--------|
214	| `Ctrl + 1..9` | Switch to window 1–9 (no prefix, requires CSI-u terminal) |
215	| `Ctrl + 0` | Jump to git root session via sesh (no prefix, requires CSI-u) |
216	| `prefix + Space` | Native popup menu (layouts, sessions, sesh, resize, etc.) |
217	| `prefix + h/j/k/l` | Navigate panes (vim-style) |
218	| `prefix + H/J/K/L` | Resize panes (5 cells) |
219	| `prefix + M-h/j/k/l` | Fine resize panes (1 cell) |
220	| `prefix + +` | Set current pane to 75% width |
221	| `prefix + \|` | Split pane left/right |
222	| `prefix + -` | Split pane top/bottom |
223	| `prefix + F` | Toggle floating pane (tmux-floax) |
224	| `prefix + P` | Floax popup menu |
225	| `prefix + u` | Open fzf URL picker (tmux-fzf-url) |
226	| `prefix + [` | Enter vim-style copy mode (v/V/y to select/yank) |
227	| `prefix + y` | Copy visible pane to clipboard |
228	| `prefix + Y` | Copy full scrollback to clipboard |
229	| `prefix + C-y` | fzf line picker from scrollback |
230	| `prefix + g` | Sesh session picker (fzf popup) |
231	| `prefix + T` | Sesh session picker (television popup) |
232	| `prefix + O` | Sesh built-in picker popup |
233	| `prefix + W` | Sesh window picker (fzf popup) |
234	| `prefix + S` | Switch to last session (sesh) |
235	| `prefix + 9` | Jump to git root session (sesh) |
236	| `prefix + N` | New session (prompts for name) |
237	| `prefix + X` | Kill session (with confirmation) |
238	| `prefix + R` | Reload tmux config |
239	| `prefix + M-c` | Switch theme to Catppuccin (top status bar) |
240	| `prefix + M-t` | Switch theme to tmux2k (bottom status bar) |
241	
242	Note: `Ctrl+Space` is NOT bound (reserved for input method switching). `Ctrl+1..9` and `Ctrl+0` require CSI-u terminal support (Ghostty/cmux, Alacritty, Kitty); legacy terminals fall back to `prefix + number`. Popup menu accelerator keys match standalone `prefix + key` bindings (see `docs/tools/tmux/keybindings.md` for full mapping).
243	
244	## Zellij Configuration
245	
246	Zellij config (`dot_config/zellij/config.kdl`) uses `default_mode "locked"` so all keys pass through to inner applications by default. Press `Ctrl+G` to unlock Zellij commands. This prevents key conflicts with coding agents and vim-style applications.
247	
248	On first Zellij launch (without existing config), select the "Unlock-First (non-colliding)" keybinding preset for the best experience.

251	
252	- Neovim >= 0.11.2
253	- ripgrep, fd
254	- Node.js (via mise on Linux, Homebrew on macOS)
255	- tree-sitter-cli
256	- lazygit, fzf (via git on Linux, Homebrew on macOS)

259	
260	After `chezmoi apply`:
261	
262	- Config files in `~/.*`
263	- Ansible playbooks in `~/.ansible/`

265	## Development
266	
267	After modifying ansible playbooks or roles, run syntax check:
268	
269	```bash
270	ANSIBLE_CONFIG=dot_ansible/ansible.cfg ansible-playbook --syntax-check dot_ansible/playbooks/base.yml
271	ANSIBLE_CONFIG=dot_ansible/ansible.cfg ansible-playbook --syntax-check dot_ansible/playbooks/macos.yml
272	ANSIBLE_CONFIG=dot_ansible/ansible.cfg ansible-playbook --syntax-check dot_ansible/playbooks/linux.yml
273	```
274	
275	## Ansible vs Homebrew
276	
277	**Primary tool: Ansible** - manages CLI tools and system dependencies cross-platform.
278	
279	| Tool | Role | When to Use |
280	|------|------|-------------|
281	| **Ansible** | CLI tools, system packages | Always (apt/brew formulas) |
282	| **Brewfile** | macOS GUI apps (casks), App Store | Optional (opt-in) |
283	| **Linuxbrew** | Linux packages not in apt | Always installed on Linux |
284	
285	**How they work together:**
286	
287	- Bootstrap installs Homebrew on both macOS and Linux
288	- Ansible roles use `community.general.homebrew` for macOS formulas
289	- Brewfile manages casks (GUI apps) and mas (App Store) separately
290	- On Linux, Ansible uses apt; Linuxbrew is available for newer packages
291	
292	## Brewfile (GUI Apps - Opt-in)
293	
294	GUI applications are managed via Homebrew Brewfile in XDG-compliant location `~/.config/homebrew/`.
295	
296	**Note**: Brewfile installation is **opt-in** (disabled by default). Enable general GUI apps via `chezmoi init --force` and set `installBrewApps = true`. On macOS, AI desktop apps are a separate opt-in via `installAiDesktopApps = true`.
297	
298	### File Structure
299	
300	```
301	~/.config/homebrew/
302	├── Brewfile          # Shared: taps, CLI formulas, mas
303	├── Brewfile.darwin   # macOS: casks (GUI apps), mas entries
304	└── Brewfile.linux    # Linux: linuxbrew-specific (minimal)
305	```
306	
307	### Usage
308	
309	```bash
310	# Edit Brewfiles
311	chezmoi edit ~/.config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin
312	
313	# Apply changes manually
314	brew bundle --file=~/.config/homebrew/Brewfile
315	brew bundle --file=~/.config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin
316	
317	# Or just run chezmoi apply (triggers run_onchange script)
318	chezmoi apply
319	
320	# Check what would be installed
321	brew bundle check --file=~/.config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin
322	```
323	
324	### Brewfile Categories (darwin)
325	
326	- **Terminals & Editors**: alacritty, iterm2, warp, cmux, cursor, visual-studio-code
327	- **AI & Coding**: claude, chatgpt, opencode-desktop, antigravity, codex-app (Apple Silicon only), and `ollama-app` when `installAiDesktopApps` + `installLlmTools`
328	- **System Utilities**: aerospace, alt-tab, raycast, jordanbaird-ice
329	- **Communication**: discord, telegram, wechat, tencent-meeting
330	- **Browsers**: arc, google-chrome, tor-browser
331	- **Productivity**: obsidian, google-drive, grammarly-desktop
332	- **Gaming**: steam, minecraft, battle-net (skipped if WORK_MACHINE env var set)
333	- **Finance**: binance, tradingview
334	- **Network**: tailscale, openvpn-connect, clash-verge-rev
335	- **Mac App Store**: LINE, Keynote, Numbers, Pages
336	
337	### Customizing Brewfile
338	
339	The Brewfiles are chezmoi templates. Conditional sections:
340	
341	- Gaming apps: skipped if `WORK_MACHINE` environment variable is set
342	- Chinese apps (baidunetdisk): only included if `useChineseMirror` is true
343	- mas apps: requires signing in to App Store.app first
344	
345	## Customization
346	
347	See [docs/ansible.md](docs/ansible.md) for detailed ansible customization guide.
348

43	_fzf_comprun() {

45	    shift
46	
47	    case "$command" in
48	        cd)
49	            if command -v eza &>/dev/null; then
50	                fzf --preview 'eza --tree --color=always {} | head -200' "$@"
51	            else

53	            fi

60	            ;;
61	        *)
62	            if command -v bat &>/dev/null; then
63	                fzf --preview 'bat -n --color=always --line-range :500 {}' "$@"
64	            else
65	                fzf --preview 'head -500 {}' "$@"
66	            fi
67	            ;;
68	    esac

1	# 22_sesh.zsh - sesh tmux session manager
2	# https://github.com/joshmedeski/sesh
3	
4	# Check if sesh is installed
5	command -v sesh &>/dev/null || return 0
6	
7	# Auto-generate shell completion into ~/.zfunc/ (regenerates on version change)
8	if [[ -d ~/.zfunc ]]; then
9	    local _sesh_ver="$(sesh --version 2>/dev/null)"
10	    if [[ ! -f ~/.zfunc/_sesh ]] || ! grep -q "${_sesh_ver}" ~/.zfunc/_sesh 2>/dev/null; then
11	        sesh completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_sesh 2>/dev/null
12	    fi
13	fi
14	
15	# Sesh session switcher with fzf (full-featured picker)
16	# Supports icons, preview, filtering by source, and session killing
17	function sesh-sessions() {
18	    {
19	        exec </dev/tty
20	        exec <&1
21	        local session
22	        session=$(sesh list --icons | fzf-tmux -p 80%,70% \
23	            --no-sort --ansi --border-label ' sesh ' --prompt '⚡  ' \
24	            --header '  ^a all ^t tmux ^g configs ^x zoxide ^d tmux kill ^f find' \
25	            --bind 'tab:down,btab:up' \
26	            --bind 'ctrl-a:change-prompt(⚡  )+reload(sesh list --icons)' \
27	            --bind 'ctrl-t:change-prompt(🪟  )+reload(sesh list -t --icons)' \
28	            --bind 'ctrl-g:change-prompt(⚙️  )+reload(sesh list -c --icons)' \
29	            --bind 'ctrl-x:change-prompt(📁  )+reload(sesh list -z --icons)' \
30	            --bind 'ctrl-f:change-prompt(🔎  )+reload(fd -H -d 2 -t d -E .Trash . ~)' \
31	            --bind 'ctrl-d:execute(tmux kill-session -t {2..})+change-prompt(⚡  )+reload(sesh list --icons)' \
32	            --preview-window 'right:55%' \
33	            --preview 'sesh preview {}' \
34	        )
35	        zle reset-prompt > /dev/null 2>&1 || true
36	        [[ -z "$session" ]] && return
37	        sesh connect "$session"
38	    }
39	}
40	
41	# Connect to a sesh session for the current directory (creates it if missing).
42	# Smart argument handling:
43	#   shere                              # default startup_command (nvim)
44	#   shere specstory run codex          # bare args → treated as command
45	#   shere -c "specstory run codex"     # explicit --command flag
46	#   shere -p ~/my-proj                 # explicit path
47	#   shere -p ~/my-proj npm run dev     # explicit path + command
48	function sesh-here() {
49	    local cmd="" path=""
50	    # Parse flags first
51	    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
52	        case "$1" in
53	            -c|--command) cmd="$2"; shift 2 ;;
54	            -p|--path)    path="$2"; shift 2 ;;
55	            -*)           echo "sesh-here: unknown flag $1" >&2; return 1 ;;
56	            *)            break ;;  # remaining args are the command
57	        esac
58	    done
59	    # Remaining positional args become the command
60	    [[ $# -gt 0 && -z "$cmd" ]] && cmd="$*"
61	    path="${path:-$PWD}"
62	    if [[ -n "$cmd" ]]; then
63	        sesh connect --command "$cmd" "$path"
64	    else
65	        sesh connect "$path"
66	    fi
67	}
68	
69	# Connect to the current git root when available, otherwise use $PWD.
70	# Same smart argument handling as sesh-here.
71	#   sroot                              # default startup_command
72	#   sroot specstory run codex          # bare args → command
73	#   sroot -c "specstory run codex"     # explicit --command flag
74	function sesh-root() {
75	    local cmd="" root
76	    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
77	        case "$1" in
78	            -c|--command) cmd="$2"; shift 2 ;;
79	            -*)           shift ;;
80	            *)            break ;;
81	        esac
82	    done
83	    [[ $# -gt 0 && -z "$cmd" ]] && cmd="$*"
84	    root=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) || root=$PWD
85	    if [[ -n "$cmd" ]]; then
86	        sesh connect --command "$cmd" "$root"
87	    else
88	        sesh connect "$root"
89	    fi
90	}
91	
92	alias shere='sesh-here'
93	alias sroot='sesh-root'
94

96	zle -N sesh-sessions
97	
98	# Key bindings (Alt+S for session switcher, avoids conflict with Ctrl+A tmux prefix)
99	bindkey -M emacs '\es' sesh-sessions
100	bindkey -M viins '\es' sesh-sessions
101	bindkey -M vicmd '\es' sesh-sessions
102

1	# 11_tools_picker.zsh - Interactive CLI tools picker (fzf ZLE widget)
2	# Reads ~/.config/docs/tools/cli-tools.md for the tool list (deployed by chezmoi).
3	#
4	# Alt+T  →  open picker
5	#   Enter      paste invocation to shell buffer (you still press Enter to run)
6	#   Ctrl+E     execute the tool directly (good for TUI apps: btop, lazygit, etc.)
7	#   Ctrl+/     toggle preview panel (shows tldr or --help)
8	#
9	# The invocation for tools that need arguments has a trailing space,
10	# so pressing Enter pastes e.g. "rg " — cursor lands after the space,
11	# ready for you to type your arguments.
12	
13	_TOOLS_DOC="${HOME}/.config/docs/tools/cli-tools.md"
14	
15	# Bail silently if the data file hasn't been deployed yet or fzf is missing
16	[[ -f "$_TOOLS_DOC" ]] || return 0
17	command -v fzf &>/dev/null || return 0
18	
19	# Parse the markdown tables into "INVOCATION<TAB>DESCRIPTION" lines.
20	# Tab separator preserves the trailing space in invocations like "rg ".
21	_tools_list() {
22	    awk -F'|' '/^[[:space:]]*\|[[:space:]]*`/ {
23	      inv=$3; sub(/^[[:space:]]*`/,"",inv); sub(/`[[:space:]]*$/,"",inv)
24	      desc=$4; sub(/^[[:space:]]*/,"",desc); sub(/[[:space:]]*$/,"",desc)
25	      printf "%s\t%s\n", inv, desc
26	    }' "$_TOOLS_DOC"
27	}
28	
29	# ZLE widget: opens fzf picker, pastes selected invocation to the shell command line.
30	tools-picker() {
31	    {
32	        exec </dev/tty
33	        exec <&1
34	
35	        local selected
36	        selected=$(
37	            _tools_list | fzf \
38	                --ansi \
39	                --border \
40	                --prompt ' tools  ' \
41	                --header 'Enter: paste  Ctrl+E: execute  Ctrl+/: preview' \
42	                --delimiter=$'\t' \
43	                --with-nth=1,2 \
44	                --preview 'tool=$(printf "%s" {1} | awk "{print \$1}" | sed "s/ *$//"); (command -v tldr >/dev/null 2>&1 && tldr "$tool" 2>/dev/null) || "$tool" --help 2>&1 | head -50' \
45	                --preview-window='right:55%:wrap:hidden' \
46	                --bind='ctrl-/:toggle-preview' \
47	                --bind='ctrl-e:execute(eval $(printf "%s" {1} | awk "{print \$1}"))+abort'
48	        )
49	
50	        zle reset-prompt >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
51	        [[ -z "$selected" ]] && return
52	
53	        # Extract the invocation (field 1 before the tab), preserving trailing space
54	        local invocation
55	        invocation=$(printf '%s' "$selected" | cut -f1)
56	
57	        # Paste to shell command line buffer without executing
58	        LBUFFER="${LBUFFER}${invocation}"
59	        zle redisplay
60	    }
61	}
62	
63	zle -N tools-picker
64	
65	# Alt+T (mnemonic: Tools)
66	# Alt+S = sesh-sessions, Alt+C = fzf cd — Alt+T is free
67	bindkey -M emacs '\et' tools-picker
68	bindkey -M viins '\et' tools-picker
69	bindkey -M vicmd '\et' tools-picker
70

```text
1	# tmux — Keybindings
2	
3	All bindings use the default prefix `Ctrl + b`.
4	
5	## Daily Workflow
6	
7	| Keybinding | Action |
8	|------------|--------|
9	| `prefix + R` | Reload `~/.tmux.conf` |
10	| `prefix + Space` | Open the tmux popup menu |
11	| `prefix + g` | Open sesh picker |
12	| `prefix + T` | Open sesh picker via television (tv) |
13	| `prefix + O` | Open sesh built-in picker |
14	| `prefix + W` | Open sesh window picker (fzf) |
15	| `prefix + S` | Jump to the last sesh session |
16	| `prefix + 9` | Jump to the git root session for the current repo |
17	| `prefix + N` | New session (prompts for name) |
18	| `prefix + X` | Kill session (with confirmation) |
19	| `prefix + d` | Detach |
20	| `prefix + t` | Show tmux clock mode |
21	| `prefix + M-c` | Switch theme to Catppuccin (top status bar) |
22	| `prefix + M-t` | Switch theme to tmux2k (bottom status bar) |
23	
24	## Panes and Windows
25	
26	| Keybinding | Action |
27	|------------|--------|
28	| `Ctrl + 1..9` | Switch to window 1–9 (requires CSI-u terminal: Ghostty, Alacritty, Kitty) |
29	| `Ctrl + 0` | Jump to git root session via sesh (same as `prefix + 9`) |
30	| `Ctrl + h/j/k/l` | Move between panes — crosses into Neovim splits (vim-tmux-navigator) |
31	| `Ctrl + \` | Focus previous pane/split (vim-tmux-navigator) |
32	| `prefix + h/j/k/l` | Move between panes (fallback, tmux-only) |
33	| `prefix + H/J/K/L` | Resize panes (5 cells, repeatable) |
34	| `prefix + M-h/j/k/l` | Fine resize panes (1 cell, repeatable) |
35	| `prefix + +` | Set current pane to 75% width |
36	| `prefix + \|` | Split left/right (vertical divider) |
37	| `prefix + -` | Split top/bottom (horizontal divider) |
38	| `prefix + c` | New window in current path |
39	| `prefix + x` | Kill pane |
40	| `prefix + z` | Toggle pane zoom |
41	| `prefix + {` | Swap pane with previous (left/up) |
42	| `prefix + }` | Swap pane with next (right/down) |
43	| `prefix + [` | Enter copy mode |
44	
45	`Ctrl+1..9` and `Ctrl+0` require CSI-u terminal support. Ghostty/cmux sends these natively. Alacritty needs explicit `keyboard.bindings` (managed by this repo in `dot_config/alacritty/alacritty.toml`). Legacy terminals (Terminal.app, plain SSH) cannot send these — use `prefix + number` instead.
46	
47	Swap-pane swaps the **content** while keeping the **sizes**. So if you have a 75%/25% split and swap, the left pane's content moves to the right (25%) and vice versa — the proportions stay fixed.
48	
49	## Layouts
50	
51	| Keybinding | Action |
52	|------------|--------|
53	| `M-1` | Even horizontal layout |
54	| `M-2` | Even vertical layout |
55	| `M-3` | Main horizontal layout |
56	| `M-4` | Main vertical layout |
57	| `M-5` | Tiled layout |
58	| `prefix + E` | Spread panes evenly (built-in) |
59	
60	`M-1` through `M-5` are tmux built-ins — no prefix needed; just hold Meta (Alt/Option) and press the number.
61	
62	> **macOS terminal requirement**: Option must send Meta/Esc+ for `M-` bindings to work. Ghostty/cmux: `macos-option-as-alt = left` (managed by this repo in `dot_config/ghostty/config`). Alacritty: `window.option_as_alt: OnlyLeft`. iTerm2: Profiles > Keys > Left Option Key > Esc+. See [docs/tools/ghostty.md](../ghostty.md).
63	
64	## Floating Pane (tmux-floax)
65	
66	| Keybinding | Action |
67	|------------|--------|
68	| `prefix + F` | Toggle floating pane (80% width/height) |
69	| `prefix + P` | Open floax popup menu |
70	
71	The floating pane uses a dedicated tmux session named `float` (hidden from sesh picker via blacklist). It inherits the current pane path. Useful for quick terminal tasks without disrupting your layout.
72	
73	## Copy Mode (Vim-Style)
74	
75	Enter with `prefix + [`. Navigate with vim keys, then:
76	
77	| Key | Action |
78	|-----|--------|
79	| `v` | Begin character selection (visual mode) |
80	| `V` | Select entire line |
81	| `C-v` | Toggle rectangle/block selection |
82	| `y` | Yank selection to system clipboard |
83	| `/` | Search forward |
84	| `?` | Search backward |
85	| `n`/`N` | Next/previous search match |
86	| `g`/`G` | Jump to top/bottom |
87	| `C-u`/`C-d` | Half-page up/down |
88	| `q` or `Escape` | Exit copy mode |
89	
90	Mouse drag in copy mode also copies to clipboard. Double-click selects a word.
91	
92	## Right-click menus
93	
94	Right-click opens a context menu depending on where you click:
95	
96	| Target | Menu |
97	|--------|------|
98	| Pane body (`MouseDown3Pane`) | Split / swap / zoom / kill / respawn |
99	| Window list (`MouseDown3Status`) | Swap / rename / kill / new window |
100	| Session area on the left (`MouseDown3StatusLeft`) | Next/prev/rename session, new session/window |
101	
102	Our bindings use `display-menu -O` so the menu stays open after the mouse button is released — pick an item or press Escape to dismiss. (tmux's defaults omit `-O` and dismiss on release, which makes the menu unusable.)
103	
104	## URL Opening
105	
106	| Keybinding | Action |
107	|------------|--------|
108	| `prefix + u` | Open fzf popup listing all URLs in the pane (tmux-fzf-url) |
109	
110	In copy-mode (after selecting text with `v`):
111	
112	| Key | Action |
113	|-----|--------|
114	| `o` | Open selected URL/file in default browser/app (tmux-open) |
115	| `C-o` | Open selection in `$EDITOR` |
116	| `S` | Search selection in Google (tmux-open, configurable via `@open-S`) |
117	
118	Typical workflow: `prefix + u` for quick URL browsing; `prefix + [` then select + `o` for precise URL opening.
119	
120	## Capture Pane
121	
122	| Keybinding | Action |
123	|------------|--------|
124	| `prefix + y` | Copy visible pane content to system clipboard |
125	| `prefix + Y` | Copy full scrollback to system clipboard |

127	
128	Cross-platform: `pbcopy` on macOS, `xclip`/`xsel` on Linux. OSC 52 also works for the vim-style `y` yank (even over SSH).

```text
1	# fzf Quick Reference
2	
3	[fzf](https://github.com/junegunn/fzf) — command-line fuzzy finder.
4	
5	Config source: `dot_config/zsh/tools/10_fzf.zsh`
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Shell Keybindings
10	
11	| Key | Action | Preview |
12	|-----|--------|---------|
13	| `Ctrl+T` | Insert fuzzy-matched file path at cursor | `bat` syntax highlight (500 lines) |
14	| `Ctrl+R` | Fuzzy search command history | — |
15	| `Alt+C` | Fuzzy-match directory and `cd` into it | `eza --tree` (200 lines) |
16	
17	---
18	
19	## Environment Variables
20	
21	```bash
22	# Base options applied to all fzf invocations
23	FZF_DEFAULT_OPTS="--height 40% --layout=reverse --border"
24	
25	# Use fd instead of find (respects .gitignore, faster)
26	FZF_DEFAULT_COMMAND="fd --hidden --strip-cwd-prefix --exclude .git"
27	
28	# Ctrl+T: file picker
29	FZF_CTRL_T_COMMAND="fd --hidden --strip-cwd-prefix --exclude .git"
30	FZF_CTRL_T_OPTS="--preview 'bat -n --color=always --line-range :500 {}'"
31	
32	# Alt+C: directory picker
33	FZF_ALT_C_COMMAND="fd --type=d --hidden --strip-cwd-prefix --exclude .git"
34	FZF_ALT_C_OPTS="--preview 'eza --tree --color=always {} | head -200'"
35	```
36	
37	---
38	
39	## Tab Completion Preview (`_fzf_comprun`)
40	
41	When using fzf-powered tab completion, preview varies by command:
42	
43	| Command | Preview |
44	|---------|---------|
45	| `cd` | `eza --tree --color=always` (fallback: `tree -C`) |
46	| `export`, `unset` | `echo ${<var>}` — shows current variable value |
47	| `ssh` | `dig <host>` — DNS lookup |
48	| *(default)* | `bat -n --color=always --line-range :500` |
49	
50	---
51	
52	## fzf-tmux Integration
53	
54	The `sesh-sessions` widget (bound to `Alt+S`) uses `fzf-tmux -p 80%,70%` to open a
55	floating popup inside tmux. See `docs/tools/sesh.md` for session picker keybindings.
56	
57	---
58	
59	## Tips
60	
61	- **Fuzzy syntax**: space-separated tokens are AND'd; `!` negates; `^` anchors start; `$` anchors end
62	  - Example: `^foo bar !baz$` — starts with "foo", contains "bar", does not end with "baz"
63	- **Multi-select**: pass `--multi` (or `-m`) to enable `Tab`/`Shift+Tab` for multi-selection
64	- **Preview toggle**: `Ctrl+/` toggles the preview pane (built-in default)
65
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	# Sesh - Smart Tmux Session Manager
2	
3	[Sesh](https://github.com/joshmedeski/sesh) is a CLI that manages tmux sessions using zoxide, giving you instant access to your most-used projects with smart session naming, startup commands, and preview.
4	
5	## Installation
6	
7	Sesh is installed automatically by the `devtools` ansible role:
8	
9	- **macOS**: `brew install sesh`
10	- **Linux**: GitHub release binary → `~/.local/bin/sesh`
11	
12	No manual installation needed after `chezmoi apply`.
13	
14	## Keybindings
15	
16	### ZSH (`Alt+S`)
17	
18	Press `Alt+S` anywhere in the shell to open the sesh picker. This uses `fzf-tmux` as a popup with full filtering support.
19	
20	Source: `~/.config/zsh/tools/22_sesh.zsh`
21	
22	### ZSH Helpers
23	
24	The managed zsh config also provides two shell helpers:
25	
26	| Command | Action |
27	|---------|--------|
28	| `shere` | Connect to a sesh session for the current directory |
29	| `sroot` | Connect to the current git root if present, otherwise `$PWD` |
30	
31	The underlying functions are `sesh-here` and `sesh-root`, so you can call them directly if you prefer function names over aliases.
32	
33	Both helpers accept a **command** as bare arguments (no quotes needed), which overrides the default `startup_command` from `sesh.toml`:
34	
35	```bash
36	# No args → default startup_command (nvim)
37	shere
38	sroot
39	
40	# Bare args → treated as the command to run in the new session
41	shere specstory run codex
42	shere npm run dev
43	sroot specstory run codex
44	
45	# Explicit flags (also supported)
46	shere -c "specstory run codex"       # --command flag
47	shere -p ~/repos/my-project          # --path flag (overrides $PWD)
48	shere -p ~/repos/my-project npm dev  # path + command
49	```
50	
51	**Note:** `--command` only takes effect when creating a new session. If the session already exists, sesh switches to it and ignores the command.
52	
53	### tmux
54	
55	All keybindings use the tmux prefix (default `Ctrl+B`).
56	
57	| Keybinding | Action |
58	|------------|--------|
59	| `prefix + g` | Open sesh picker popup (fzf with preview, icons, filtering) |
60	| `prefix + T` | Open sesh picker via television (tv) in a tmux popup |
61	| `prefix + O` | Open sesh built-in picker in a tmux popup |
62	| `prefix + W` | Open sesh window picker (fzf) -- switch or create tmux windows |
63	| `prefix + S` | Switch to last session (via `sesh last`) |
64	| `prefix + 9` | Jump to root of current git repo/worktree |
65	
66	Source: `~/.tmux.conf`
67	
68	`prefix + g` avoids relying on `Shift`, so it does not fall through to tmux's built-in `prefix + t` clock shortcut on terminals that do not report uppercase prefix bindings reliably.
69	
70	### Picker Keybindings (inside fzf popup)
71	
72	| Key | Action |
73	|-----|--------|
74	| `Ctrl+A` | Show all sessions |
75	| `Ctrl+T` | Filter: tmux sessions only |
76	| `Ctrl+G` | Filter: configured sessions only |
77	| `Ctrl+X` | Filter: zoxide directories only |
78	| `Ctrl+F` | Filter: find directories (`fd`) |
79	| `Ctrl+D` | Kill selected tmux session |
80	| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Navigate down/up |
81	
82	## Shell Completion
83	
84	ZSH tab completion for `sesh` subcommands and flags is auto-generated into `~/.zfunc/_sesh` on first load (and regenerated when sesh version changes). This follows the project's [completion pattern](zsh/zsh-completions.md).
85	
86	Manual regeneration:
87	
88	```bash
89	sesh completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_sesh
90	rm -f ~/.zcompdump && compinit
91	```
92	
93	## Configuration
94	
95	Config file: `~/.config/sesh/sesh.toml` (managed by chezmoi)
96	
97	### Schema Autocomplete
98	
99	The config includes a JSON Schema directive for editor autocomplete via [taplo](https://taplo.tamasfe.dev/):
100	
101	```toml
102	#:schema https://github.com/joshmedeski/sesh/raw/main/sesh.schema.json
103	```
104	
105	### Key Options
106	
107	| Option | Description |
108	|--------|-------------|
109	| `sort_order` | Session type display order: `tmux`, `config`, `tmuxinator`, `zoxide` |
110	| `dir_length` | Directory components in session names (default: 1) |
111	| `blacklist` | Regex patterns to hide from the picker |
112	| `cache` | Enable stale-while-revalidate caching (experimental) |
113	
114	### Default Session
115	
116	Applied to all sessions unless overridden:
117	
118	```toml
119	[default_session]
120	startup_command = "nvim"
121	preview_command = "eza --all --git --icons --color=always {}"
122	```
123	
124	- `startup_command`: runs when a new session is created
125	- `preview_command`: shown in the fzf preview pane (`{}` = session path)
126	
127	### Named Sessions
128	
129	Pin frequently used directories with custom names and commands:
130	
131	```toml
132	[[session]]
133	name = "chezmoi"
134	path = "~/.local/share/chezmoi"
135	tmuxinator = "chezmoi"    # delegates to tmuxinator for reliable multi-window setup
136	
137	[[session]]
138	name = "home"
139	path = "~"
140	disable_startup_command = true
141	```
142	
143	Available fields: `name`, `path`, `startup_command`, `preview_command`, `disable_startup_command`, `windows`.
144	
145	### Wildcard Sessions
146	
147	Apply settings to directories matching a glob pattern:
148	
149	```toml
150	[[wildcard]]
151	pattern = "~/repos/*"
152	startup_command = "nvim"
153	```
154	
155	- `*` matches one level, `**` matches recursively
156	- Explicit `[[session]]` entries take priority over wildcards
157	
158	### Windows
159	
160	Define reusable window layouts:
161	
162	```toml
163	[[session]]
164	name = "my-project"
165	path = "~/repos/my-project"
166	windows = ["git"]
167	
168	[[window]]
169	name = "git"
170	startup_script = "lazygit"
171	```
172	
173	## Recommended tmux Settings
174	
175	These are already set in `~/.tmux.conf`:
176	
177	```
178	set -g detach-on-destroy off   # stay in tmux when closing a session
179	bind-key x kill-pane           # skip kill-pane confirmation
180	```
181	
182	## Integration with Other Tools
183	
184	### fzf
185	
186	Sesh's primary picker integration. The `fzf-tmux` wrapper renders fzf inside a tmux popup. Our setup uses `--icons` for Nerd Font glyphs and `sesh preview` for the preview pane.
187	
188	### zoxide
189	
190	Sesh uses zoxide's frecency database to suggest directories. Any directory you `cd` into is automatically tracked and appears in `sesh list -z`.
191	
192	### Television (tv)
193	
194	[Television](https://github.com/alexpasmantier/television) has a built-in [sesh channel](https://alexpasmantier.github.io/television/community/channels-unix/#sesh). Television is installed by the `devtools` ansible role (`brew install television` on macOS, GitHub release binary on Linux).
195	
196	**tmux keybinding:** `prefix + T` opens television's sesh channel in a tmux popup.
197	
198	```
199	bind-key "T" display-popup -E -w 80% -h 70% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' Sesh (tv) ' "tv sesh"
200	```
201	
202	Use `Ctrl-s` to cycle through sources (all, tmux, config, zoxide, fd), and `Ctrl-d` to kill the highlighted session.
203	
204	A custom cable channel config at `~/.config/television/cable/sesh.toml` overrides the built-in channel with richer source cycling and actions matching our fzf picker setup.
205	
206	### Raycast (macOS)
207	
208	The [sesh Raycast extension](https://www.raycast.com/joshmedeski/sesh) provides GUI-based session switching outside the terminal.
209	
210	## Customization Tips
211	
212	1. **Add project sessions**: Edit `~/.config/sesh/sesh.toml` (via `chezmoi edit ~/.config/sesh/sesh.toml`) to pin your most-used projects.
213	
214	2. **Wildcard for monorepos**: Use `pattern = "~/work/monorepo/packages/*"` to auto-configure all sub-projects.
215	
216	3. **Per-project startup**: Set `startup_command` to launch dev servers, editors, or TUI tools automatically.
217	
218	4. **Preview with bat**: Use `preview_command = "bat --color=always {}/README.md"` to show project READMEs in the picker.
219	
220	5. **Multiple windows**: Define `[[window]]` entries and reference them in sessions for multi-pane layouts (e.g., editor + lazygit).
221	
222	## Pane Layouts (Advanced)
223	
224	### Sesh Limitations
225	
226	Sesh **cannot** create pane splits natively. Each `[[window]]` gets exactly one pane with one `startup_script`. There is no `panes`, `layout`, `size`, or `ratio` configuration.
227	
228	If you need predefined pane layouts (e.g., "left pane = nvim 75%, right pane = specstory run 25%"), you must use an external tool.
229	
230	### The `tmuxp` Field is Dead Code (as of sesh v2.24)
231	
232	**Important**: The `tmuxp` field in `sesh.toml` (on `[[session]]` and `[default_session]`) is defined in the Go struct and JSON schema, but **never read or used** by sesh's source code. Only `tmuxinator` has a working integration.
233	
234	Evidence from source code:
235	- `startup/config.go` checks `Tmuxinator` and `StartupCommand` but **not** `Tmuxp`
236	- `connector/connect.go` has a `tmuxinatorStrategy` but **no** `tmuxpStrategy`
237	- Setting `tmuxp = "..."` in sesh.toml does nothing -- the session falls through to `default_session.startup_command`
238	
239	### Approach B: tmuxp via `startup_command` (Active)
240	
241	Use sesh's `startup_command` to call `tmuxp load --append`, which appends windows from a tmuxp YAML into the sesh-created session, then kill the initial empty window.
242	
243	Config in `sesh.toml`:
244	```toml
245	[[session]]
246	name = "coding-agent"
247	path = "~"
248	startup_command = "tmuxp load -a -y ~/.config/tmuxp/coding-agent.yaml && tmux kill-window -t coding-agent:1"
249	```
250	
251	Layout defined in `~/.config/tmuxp/coding-agent.yaml`:
252	```yaml
253	session_name: coding-agent
254	windows:
255	  - window_name: editor
256	    layout: main-vertical
257	    options:
258	      main-pane-width: 75%    # 3:1 ratio
259	    panes:
260	      - shell_command: nvim
261	      - shell_command: specstory run
262	  - window_name: monitor
263	    panes:
264	      - shell_command: btop
265	```
266	
267	**How it works:**
268	1. `sesh connect coding-agent` → sesh creates a tmux session named `coding-agent` at `~`
269	2. `startup_command` runs inside the first pane via `tmux send-keys`
270	3. `tmuxp load -a -y` appends the "editor" and "monitor" windows to the current session
271	4. `tmux kill-window -t coding-agent:1` removes the initial empty window sesh created
272	
273	**Pros:** tmuxp already installed, declarative YAML, `--append` avoids session conflict.
274	**Cons:** brief flash of empty window being killed; `startup_command` is `send-keys` so timing-sensitive.
275	
276	**Requires:** `tmuxp` (`pip install tmuxp` or `uv tool install tmuxp`)
277	
278	### Approach C: tmuxinator Native Integration (Alternative)
279	
280	Sesh has full native support for tmuxinator. When `tmuxinator` field is set, sesh **bypasses** its own `NewSession` + `startup.Exec` and delegates entirely to `tmuxinator start`.
281	
282	Config in `sesh.toml`:
283	```toml
284	[[session]]
285	name = "coding-agent"
286	path = "~"
287	tmuxinator = "coding-agent"
288	```
289	
290	Layout defined in `~/.config/tmuxinator/coding-agent.yml`:
291	```yaml
292	name: coding-agent
293	root: <%= @settings["root"] || "~" %>
294	on_project_start: tmux set-window-option main-pane-width 75%
295	windows:
296	  - editor:
297	      layout: main-vertical
298	      panes:
299	        - nvim
300	        - specstory run
301	  - monitor:
302	      panes:
303	        - btop
304	```
305	
306	**How it works:**
307	1. `sesh connect coding-agent` → sesh detects `tmuxinator` field
308	2. `connector/tmuxinator.go` calls `tmuxinator start coding-agent` directly
309	3. tmuxinator creates the entire session with all windows and panes
310	4. sesh then switches/attaches to the session
311	
312	**Pros:** cleanest integration, no empty window hack, sesh natively manages the lifecycle.
313	**Cons:** requires tmuxinator (`gem install tmuxinator`), Ruby dependency.
314	
315	**Requires:** `tmuxinator` (installed by `ruby_gem_tools` ansible role)
316	
317	### Approach A: Pure Shell Script (Fallback)
318	
319	For environments without tmuxp or tmuxinator, use raw tmux commands:
320	
321	```toml
322	[[session]]
323	name = "coding-agent"
324	path = "~"
325	startup_command = "tmux split-window -h -p 25 'specstory run' && tmux select-pane -L && tmux new-window -n monitor 'btop' && tmux select-window -t 1 && nvim"
326	```
327	
328	**Pros:** zero extra dependencies.
329	**Cons:** fragile, hard to read, hard to maintain.
330	
331	### Comparing Approaches
332	
333	Both `coding-agent` (tmuxp) and `coding-agent-mux` (tmuxinator) are configured in `sesh.toml` for A/B comparison:
334	
335	```bash
336	sesh connect coding-agent       # Approach B: tmuxp --append
337	sesh connect coding-agent-mux   # Approach C: tmuxinator native
338	```
339	
340	After testing, keep the one you prefer and remove/comment the other.
341	
342	## try + sesh Integration
343	
344	[try-cli](https://github.com/tobi/try) creates ephemeral project workspaces under `~/src/tries/`. A sesh wildcard automatically applies `startup_command = "nvim"` to any try project.
345	
346	### Usage
347	
348	```bash
349	# One-step: open project and start coding session
350	try-sesh some-project
351	try-sesh https://github.com/user/repo
352	
353	# Two-step: try first, then sesh
354	try some-project
355	shere                    # sesh connect "$PWD"
356	```
357	
358	The `try-sesh` function (alias: `tsesh`) runs `try` then immediately `sesh connect "$PWD"`. Session names follow `dir_length=2` convention: `tries/2026-04-14-some-project`.
359	
360	Source: `~/.config/zsh/tools/32_try.zsh`
361	
362	## Upstream Issues (tmuxp)
363	
364	Sesh's `tmuxp` config field is documented in the schema and README, but **not implemented** in the source code. Relevant upstream issues:
365	
366	- [#87 - Add tmuxp support](https://github.com/joshmedeski/sesh/issues/87) -- Feature request to add tmuxp support. Status: Closed (marked "Done" on project board), but the implementation only added the field to the config struct/schema without wiring it into the connect/startup logic.
367	- [#198 - Built-in Window and Pane management](https://github.com/joshmedeski/sesh/issues/198) -- Request for native pane/window layout support (avoiding tmuxp/tmuxinator dependency). Status: Closed. Sesh v2.25 added basic window support but still no pane splits.
368	- [#188 - startup_command sent too early](https://github.com/joshmedeski/sesh/issues/188) -- Bug where startup_command is sent before the shell is ready. Status: Open. This can affect Approach B (`tmuxp load -a`) if there's a timing issue.
369

1	# tmux × Vim / Neovim
2	
3	## Vi copy / scroll — already on
4	
5	The current config sets `mode-keys vi`, so scroll and copy mode behave vim-style out of the box:
6	
7	| Key | Action |
8	|-----|--------|
9	| `prefix + [` | Enter copy mode |
10	| `h/j/k/l` | Move cursor |
11	| `C-u` / `C-d` | Half-page up/down |
12	| `g` / `G` | Top / bottom |
13	| `/` / `?` | Search forward / backward |
14	| `v` / `V` / `C-v` | Char / line / rectangle selection |
15	| `y` | Yank to system clipboard (OSC 52) |
16	| `q` or `Escape` | Exit |
17	
18	See [keybindings.md → Copy Mode](./keybindings.md#copy-mode-vim-style) for the full table.
19	
20	## Neovim-friendly settings already in `common.conf`
21	
22	- `escape-time 0` — no ESC delay, Neovim feels responsive.
23	- `focus-events on` — Vim's `autoread` and Neovim's `FocusGained` / `FocusLost` fire correctly.
24	- `default-terminal tmux-256color` + `terminal-features ...:RGB` — true color inside tmux.
25	- `extended-keys always` + `extended-keys-format csi-u` — `Ctrl+/`, `Shift+Enter`, `Ctrl+Enter` etc. reach Neovim through tmux.
26	- `set-clipboard on` — OSC 52 yanks from copy mode work over SSH.
27	- `allow-passthrough on` — helps terminal image protocols and similar passthrough features.
28	
29	If `Ctrl+/` still does not work after `prefix + R`, restart the terminal app or `tmux kill-server` once so terminal capability negotiation is fresh. The managed Alacritty config sends `Ctrl+/` as `\u001f`, which matches LazyVim's built-in `<C-_>` fallback for terminal toggle.
30	
31	## vim-tmux-navigator
32	
33	[`christoomey/vim-tmux-navigator`](https://github.com/christoomey/vim-tmux-navigator) is installed. Prefix-less `Ctrl+h/j/k/l` moves between panes, transparently crossing tmux pane boundaries and Neovim splits:
34	
35	| Key | Action |
36	|-----|--------|
37	| `Ctrl+h` | Focus left (tmux pane or vim split) |
38	| `Ctrl+j` | Focus down |
39	| `Ctrl+k` | Focus up |
40	| `Ctrl+l` | Focus right |
41	| `Ctrl+\` | Focus previous (last-visited) |
42	
43	The Neovim spec lives at [`dot_config/nvim/lua/exact_plugins/vim-tmux-navigator.lua`](../../../dot_config/nvim/lua/exact_plugins/vim-tmux-navigator.lua); the matching tmux-side `is_vim` bindings live in [`dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf`](../../../dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf). The existing `prefix + h/j/k/l` bindings are kept as a fallback — nothing is removed.
44	
45	### Caveats
46	
47	- `Ctrl+h` is historically Backspace in some terminals. If `<BS>` misbehaves in Neovim after this, remap `<C-h>` inside Neovim insert mode or update your terminal's keyboard protocol to csi-u (already enabled in our tmux config via `extended-keys-format csi-u`).
48	- `Ctrl+\` may clash with other apps (e.g. some debuggers use it as a signal). Avoid pressing it inside those apps.
49	- If you run a nested tmux session, the outer tmux eats the Ctrl+h/j/k/l and they don't reach Neovim. Use `prefix + h/j/k/l` inside nested sessions.
50

## Comprehensive Keyboard Shortcuts Summary

Based on my thorough exploration of the chezmoi dotfiles repo, here's a complete structured report of all keyboard shortcuts/keybindings:

---

### TMUX (Ctrl+B Prefix)

#### Prefix Bindings - Daily Workflow
| Binding | Action |
|---------|--------|
| `prefix + R` | Reload `~/.tmux.conf` |
| `prefix + Space` | Open tmux popup menu (see Popup Menu section) |
| `prefix + g` | Open sesh session picker (fzf popup) |
| `prefix + T` | Open sesh picker via television (tv) popup |
| `prefix + O` | Open sesh built-in picker popup |
| `prefix + W` | Open sesh window picker (fzf) |
| `prefix + S` | Switch to last session (via sesh) |
| `prefix + 9` | Jump to git root session for current repo |
| `prefix + N` | New session (prompts for name) |
| `prefix + X` | Kill session (with confirmation) |
| `prefix + d` | Detach |
| `prefix + t` | Show tmux clock mode |
| `prefix + M-c` | Switch theme to Catppuccin (top status bar) |
| `prefix + M-t` | Switch theme to tmux2k (bottom status bar) |

#### Panes and Windows
| Binding | Action |
|---------|--------|
| `Ctrl+1..9` | Switch to window 1-9 (no prefix, requires CSI-u terminal) |
| `Ctrl+0` | Jump to git root session via sesh (no prefix) |
| `Ctrl+h/j/k/l` | Move between panes — crosses tmux/vim splits (no prefix, vim-tmux-navigator) |
| `Ctrl+\` | Focus previous pane (vim-tmux-navigator) |
| `prefix + h/j/k/l` | Move between panes (vim-style, fallback) |
| `prefix + H/J/K/L` | Resize panes (5 cells, repeatable) |
| `prefix + M-h/j/k/l` | Fine resize panes (1 cell, repeatable) |
| `prefix + +` | Set current pane to 75% width |
| `prefix + \|` | Split left/right (vertical divider) |
| `prefix + -` | Split top/bottom (horizontal divider) |
| `prefix + c` | New window in current path |
| `prefix + x` | Kill pane |
| `prefix + z` | Toggle pane zoom |
| `prefix + {` | Swap pane with previous (left/up) |
| `prefix + }` | Swap pane with next (right/down) |
| `prefix + [` | Enter copy mode |

#### Layouts (Meta/Alt + number, no prefix)

|---------|--------|

| `M-2` | Even vertical layout |

| `y` | Yank selection to system clipboard |
| `/` | Search forward |
| `?` | Search backward |
| `n`/`N` | Next/previous search match |
| `g`/`G` | Jump to top/bottom |
| `C-u`/`C-d` | Half-page up/down |
| `h/j/k/l` | Move cursor (vim-style) |
| `q` or `Escape` | Exit copy mode |

|---------|--------|
| `prefix + y` | Copy visible pane content to system clipboard |
| `prefix + Y` | Copy full scrollback to system clipboard |

#### URL Opening

| `Ctrl+T` | Filter: tmux sessions only |
| `Ctrl+G` | Filter: configured sessions only |
| `Ctrl+X` | Filter: zoxide directories only |
| `Ctrl+F` | Filter: find directories (`fd`) |
| `Ctrl+D` | Kill selected tmux session |
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Navigate down/up |

#### Tools Picker
| Binding | Widget | Mode | Action |
|---------|--------|------|--------|
| `Alt+T` | `tools-picker` | Emacs, Vi-insert, Vi-command | Open CLI tools picker (fzf popup) |

**Picker keybindings (inside fzf):**
| Key | Action |
|-----|--------|
| `Enter` | Paste selected tool invocation to shell buffer (you still press Enter to run) |
| `Ctrl+E` | Execute the tool directly (good for TUI apps: btop, lazygit, etc.) |
| `Ctrl+/` | Toggle preview panel (shows tldr or --help) |

### fzf Shell Keybindings

| Key | Action | Context |
|-----|--------|---------|
| `Ctrl+T` | Insert fuzzy-matched file path at cursor | Any shell prompt |
| `Ctrl+R` | Fuzzy search command history | Any shell prompt |
| `Alt+C` | Fuzzy-match directory and `cd` into it | Any shell prompt |

**Preview sources:**
- `Ctrl+T`: `bat` syntax highlighting (500 lines)
- `Alt+C`: `eza --tree` (200 lines)
- `Ctrl+R`: Command history (no preview)

**fzf Tab Completion Preview** (`_fzf_comprun`):
| Command | Preview |
|---------|---------|
| `cd` | `eza --tree --color=always` (or `tree -C`) |
| `export`, `unset` | Variable value via `echo ${<var>}` |
| `ssh` | DNS lookup via `dig <host>` |
| *(default)* | `bat -n --color=always --line-range :500` |

### Zellij Configuration

**Zellij starts in locked mode** — all keys pass through to inner applications by default.

| Key | Action |
|-----|--------|
| `Ctrl+G` | Unlock Zellij commands (default "Unlock-First" preset) |

**Note:** On first Zellij launch (without existing config), the setup wizard offers keybinding presets. Select "Unlock-First (non-colliding)" to avoid key conflicts with coding agents and vim-style applications. The config file is minimal and intentionally avoids defining custom keybindings beyond the unlock key.

To switch presets later:
- Default preset: `Ctrl+O` → `c`
- Unlock-First preset: `Ctrl+G` → `o` → `c`

**Settings:**
- `default_mode "locked"` — keys pass through by default
- `support_kitty_keyboard_protocol true` — proper Shift+Enter, Ctrl+Enter, etc.
- `session_serialization true` — session persistence like tmux-resurrect
- `mouse_mode true` — mouse support enabled

# Keyboard Shortcuts

Quick reference for all custom keybindings across tmux, zsh ZLE widgets, and fzf.

For deep dives: [tmux keybindings](tools/tmux/keybindings.md) · [tmux themes](tools/tmux/themes.md) · [fzf](tools/fzf.md) · [tv](tools/tv.md)

---

## tmux

Prefix key: `Ctrl+B`

### Panes & Windows

| Binding | Action |
|---------|--------|
| `Ctrl+1..9` | Switch to window 1–9 *(no prefix, requires CSI-u terminal)* |
| `Ctrl+0` | Jump to git root session via sesh *(no prefix, CSI-u)* |
| `Ctrl+h/j/k/l` | Move across panes **and** Neovim splits seamlessly |
| `prefix + h/j/k/l` | Navigate panes (vim-style fallback) |
| `prefix + H/J/K/L` | Resize pane (5 cells) |
| `prefix + M-h/j/k/l` | Fine-resize pane (1 cell) |
| `prefix + \|` | Split left/right |
| `prefix + -` | Split top/bottom |
| `prefix + +` | Set pane to 75% width |
| `prefix + z` | Zoom/unzoom pane |
| `prefix + x` | Kill pane |
| `prefix + c` | New window |
| `prefix + X` | Kill session (confirm) |
| `prefix + N` | New session (prompted) |

### Copy Mode  *(enter with `prefix + [`)*

| Key | Action |
|-----|--------|
| `v` / `V` | Begin char / line selection |
| `C-v` | Rectangle selection |
| `y` | Yank to clipboard |
| `/` / `?` | Search forward / backward |
| `g` / `G` | Jump to top / bottom |
| `C-u` / `C-d` | Half-page up / down |
| `q` | Exit copy mode |

### Clipboard Helpers

| Binding | Action |
|---------|--------|
| `prefix + y` | Copy visible pane to clipboard |
| `prefix + Y` | Copy full scrollback to clipboard |
| `prefix + C-y` | fzf line picker from scrollback |

### URL & Sessions

| Binding | Action |
|---------|--------|
| `prefix + u` | fzf URL picker (tmux-fzf-url) |
| `prefix + g` | Sesh session picker (fzf popup) |
| `prefix + T` | Sesh picker via tv (television popup) |
| `prefix + O` | Sesh built-in picker popup |
| `prefix + W` | Sesh window picker (fzf) |
| `prefix + S` | Switch to last session |
| `prefix + 9` | Jump to git root session |
| `prefix + U` | CLI tools picker (tv tools popup) |

### Themes & Config

| Binding | Action |
|---------|--------|
| `prefix + M-c` | Switch to Catppuccin theme (top status bar) |
| `prefix + M-t` | Switch to tmux2k theme (bottom status bar) |
| `prefix + R` | Reload tmux config |

### Popup Menu  *(`prefix + Space`)*

One-key access to all major operations. Accelerator letters match the standalone bindings above.

| Key | Action |
|-----|--------|
| `\|` / `-` | Split pane |
| `h/j/k/l` | Navigate panes |
| `z` | Zoom toggle |
| `c` | New window |
| `N` / `X` | New / kill session |
| `E/e/v/b/T` | Layout presets (even-h/v, main-v/h, tiled) |
| `g` / `V` / `O` | Sesh pickers (fzf / tv / built-in) |
| `W` / `S` / `9` | Sesh window / last / root |
| `B` | CLI tools picker (tv tools) |
| `C` / `M` | Theme: Catppuccin / tmux2k |
| `R` / `I` / `U` | Reload config / TPM install / TPM update |
| `?` | List all tmux keys |

> `Ctrl+Space` is intentionally unbound — reserved for input method switching.

## Zsh ZLE Widgets

Interactive pickers that open at the shell prompt without leaving the current line.

| Binding | Widget | Behavior |
|---------|--------|----------|
| `Alt+T` | `tools-picker` | CLI tools list; **Enter** pastes invocation to buffer, **Ctrl+E** executes |
| `Alt+S` | `sesh-sessions` | Sesh session switcher (same as `prefix + g` but in-shell) |
| `Alt+C` | fzf cd | Fuzzy `cd` into a directory (built-in fzf) |
| `Ctrl+T` | fzf file | Insert fuzzy-matched file path at cursor |
| `Ctrl+R` | fzf history | Fuzzy search shell history |

### Inside `tools-picker` (Alt+T)

| Key | Action |
|-----|--------|
| `Enter` | Paste invocation to buffer (safe — runs when you press Enter again) |
| `Ctrl+E` | Execute tool directly (for safe TUI tools: `btop`, `lazygit`, etc.) |
| `Ctrl+/` | Toggle preview (tldr or `--help`) |

### Inside `sesh-sessions` (Alt+S)

| Key | Action |
|-----|--------|
| `Ctrl+A/T/G/X/F` | Filter: all / tmux / configured / zoxide / find |
| `Ctrl+D` | Kill selected tmux session |

---

## tv (Television)

| Command | Binding | Action |
|---------|---------|--------|
| `tv tools` | `prefix + U` (tmux) | CLI tools picker; Enter executes, preview shows tldr |
| `tv sesh` | `prefix + T` (tmux) | Sesh session picker; Enter connects |

### Inside any tv picker

| Key | Action |
|-----|--------|
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Navigate results |
| `Ctrl+P` / `Ctrl+N` | Move up / down |
| `Ctrl+D` | Kill session *(sesh channel only)* |

## Zellij

Default mode is **locked** — all keys pass through to inner apps.

| Binding | Action |
|---------|--------|
| `Ctrl+G` | Unlock Zellij command mode |

> On first launch, select **"Unlock-First (non-colliding)"** preset to avoid conflicts with Neovim and coding agents.

---

## macOS Notes

- `M-` bindings (e.g. `M-c`, `M-t`, `Alt+T`) require your terminal to send **Option as Meta/Esc+**.
  - **Ghostty** / **cmux**: `macos-option-as-alt = left` (managed in `dot_config/ghostty/config`)
  - **iTerm2**: Preferences → Profiles → Keys → Left Option: `Esc+`
- `Ctrl+1..9` and `Ctrl+0` require **CSI-u** terminal support (Ghostty, cmux, Alacritty, Kitty).

Committed. The new **Unix Shell** section covers four groups:

- **Cursor movement** — `Ctrl+A/E` (line start/end), `Alt+F/B` (word jump), `Ctrl+XX` (toggle position)
- **Edit/Delete** — `Ctrl+W/K/U` (kill word/to-end/to-start), `Ctrl+Y`/`Alt+Y` (yank + kill-ring rotate), word case transforms (`Alt+U/L/C`)
- **History** — `Ctrl+R/P/N`, `Alt+.` (last arg, repeatable), `!!`/`!$` expansions
- **Process control** — `Ctrl+C/Z/D/L`, `Ctrl+S/Q` (XON/XOFF)

There's also a callout at the bottom noting which defaults this config overrides with ZLE widgets (`Ctrl+R`, `Ctrl+T`, `Alt+C`, `Alt+T`, `Alt+S`).
